subject: [ez4r] Announcing package afex: another car::Anova wrapper (and more)

messages.author: 2ffa956ce2411d70
messages.subject: [ez4r] Announcing package afex: another car::Anova wrapper (and more)
parts:
Dear Mike and list,

I am happy to announce that my new package “afex” has been accepted on CRAN that was heavily inspired by ez and your work and offers some similar but distinct functionality as ez. Hence, I announce it here.

Its core functions offer a way to fit ANOVA and ANCOVA models wrapping car::Anova. Function ez.glm() has an ezANOVA like interface, function aov.car() has a formula interface imitating stats::aov().
One of the distinct features of afex is that these functions return the same object as car::Anova(). So one needs to wrap the output into function univariate() or use summary(…, multivariate = FALSE) from car to obtain the univariate instead of the multivariate tests.

Furthermore, function nice.anova() produces an almost publication ready ANOVA table (however, currently without any effect size measure) from an object returned by ez.glm, aov.car or car::Anova.

Additionally, afex is set up in a way (type 3 tests as defaults and setting default contrasts to contr.sum) to replicate results from commercial software packages with the hope to ease the transition from such software to R.

Finally, afex contains the function mixed() that calculates p-values for all fixed effects (terms) in a mixed model using the Kenward-Rogers approximation for degrees of freedom implemented in pbkrtest::KRmodcomp (after fitting all the necessary models for this step using lme4::lmer).
In the current version (0.2-26, the last number denotes the r-forge revision it is based on) mixed() only allows to obtain type 3 tests for mixed models, but future versions will allow type 2 tests.

More information on afex can be found on CRAN (http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/afex/index.html) and on its homepage (which currently only focuses on the ANOVA and ANCOVA functionality): http://www.psychologie.uni-freiburg.de/Members/singmann/R/afex

As many of the ideas in afex are based on my work with ez in the last two years, I also want to say thanks for the great work and the inspirations brought by your software.

Cheers,
Henrik
